item.title: The Sonoma County Fair — Sun Aug 16, 10:00 AM — Sonoma County Fairgrounds
item.description:
A celebration of community spirit, agriculture, entertainment, and wholesome fun.
The Sonoma County Fair is an annual event that captivates visitors with its vibrant atmosphere and diverse offerings. Held in scenic Sonoma County, California, this fair is a celebration of community spirit, agriculture, entertainment, and wholesome fun. From thrilling amusement rides and live music performances to engaging exhibits showcasing local produce, crafts, and artwork, the fair offers something for everyone. Attendees can indulge in mouthwatering fair food, participate in thrilling competitions, enjoy live animal exhibits, and explore the region’s rich agricultural heritage. With its charming blend of entertainment and education, the Sonoma County Fair is a must-visit destination that brings joy and excitement to people of all ages.
Source: GoLocal Cooperative

item.title: Broadway Under the Stars - Mamma Mia! — Sun Aug 16, 7:00 PM — Sonoma Valley Field of Dreams
item.description:
The global smash hit is coming to Sonoma for the very first time! Set on a sun-drenched Greek island, Mamma Mia! follows a young bride-to-be on a quest to discover the identity of her father — bringing three very unexpected guests from her mother’s past back into their lives. Fueled by ABBA’s greatest hits (including “Dancing Queen,” “Mamma Mia,” “The Winner Takes It All,” and more), this joyful tale of family, friendship, love, and second chances has captured the hearts of millions worldwide. With its large cast, explosive dance numbers, nonstop humor, and irresistible score, Mamma Mia! promises to be one of the biggest and most unforgettable productions in Transcendence history. Mamma Mia! is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.mtishows.com
Source: GoLocal Cooperative

item.description:
This series of short, practical talks is designed to give mothers and caregivers simple, actionable tools to support their financial security, physical health, and mental well-being. Each session is 15 minutes or less and focuses on one key topic participants can immediately put into practice. Topics include: Money for Moms - Understanding Social Security benefits and simple strategies to strengthen future retirement income while raising young children. Stress Relief & Pelvic Stability Through Breathwork - A five-minute breathing routine to reduce stress and support pelvic and postural health. Fighting Anemia & Essential Postpartum Health Checks - Important information on anemia, iron and ferritin levels, Vitamin D, thyroid health, and other key postpartum screenings.

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Aug 20, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org

item.title: Craft & Chat (+ Potluck!) at Hessel Grange — Thu Aug 20, 5:30 PM — Hessel Grange
item.description: Calling all crafters, makers, artists, potluck lovers—or anyone simply looking for a reason to get out of the house and gather with community. ✺ Next Thursday, August 20th, we’re opening the doors of Hessel Grange for our first Craft + Chat + Potluck Night! Bring whatever you’re working on (or something you’ve been wanting to try)—knitting, crochet, embroidery, mending, painting, sketching, beading, carving, collage… truly, anything goes. You’re also more than welcome to come without a craft and simply share some food and good conversation. The idea is simple: bring a project, bring a dish if you can, and come spend an evening making things alongside your neighbors. item.title: A Reading in English and Spanish with Mónica de la Fuente​ — Thu Aug 20, 7:00 PM — Many Rivers Books & Tea
item.description:
Do you remember what it felt like when someone read to you as a child? ¿Requerdas como te sentias cuando eras niño y alguien te leia? ​ Many Rivers Books & Tea invites English- and Spanish-speaking families to join local author Mónica de la Fuente for an interactive reading of her mindfulness picture book, “Something in My View”. More than a traditional story time, this event will be a shared experience for children and the grown-ups who love reading to them. ​ At first glance, the book is a simple story about bubbles. As the story unfolds, children and adults are invited to discover something unexpected through curiosity, conversation, and reflection. Following the reading, children will enjoy a bubble-inspired art activity. Something in My View was inspired by Mónica’s many years of meditation practice and a desire to offer children – and the adults who read with them — a simple way to pause, share a quiet moment together, and notice what remains in that stillness. ​
Source: Seba

item.title: Pomo Cultural Series- Special Addition! — Fri Aug 21, 6:00 PM — Soper-Reese Theatre
item.description: Papa Quail Pomo Basket Project Forty years ago, I did my dissertation on Pomo Baskets. In the process I photographed 1200 baskets form major museums and private collections where I knew the village the baskets came from and in many some cases the names of the weavers. These photos focused on the Pomo baskets but also included surrounding tribes. The baskets ranged from the late 1800s to the 1980s. I also got to work with famous weavers such as Mabel McKay and Elsey Allen. As well as worked with Ramona McCloud, Joann McCloud, Frances McDaniel, Magie Carpenter, Susye Billy and Francis Jack. Now that I have retired from Fresno State, I am returning to this research to digitize these photos. I would like to return this resource to the weaving communities – long overdue. It is my pleaser to share these pictures and make available digital copies of the pictures. Just to give you a taste of the collection’s richness.
